findings.summary: An autoregressive model represents a stochastic process where each output variable depends linearly on its own prior values, forming a difference equation driven by white noise. It serves as a foundational component of ARMA and ARIMA time series frameworks, with extensions like time-varying autoregressive models accommodating non-stationary dynamics. Stationarity requires root constraints outside the unit circle; otherwise, effects persist or diverge. Shocks propagate infinitely forward, decaying geometrically when stationary. While classical AR models are linear, large language models adopt the autoregressive label without linear dependence.

mechanisms.title: Linear dependence on prior values
mechanisms.explanation: The model specifies output variables that are dependent linearly on their own previous values on a stochastic basis, expressed as a stochastic difference equation where current output is a weighted sum of lagged outputs plus white noise innovation.

mechanisms.title: Infinite impulse response from shocks
mechanisms.explanation: A one-time shock affects the evolving variable infinitely far into the future; the effect diminishes toward zero over time if the process is stationary, but persists indefinitely otherwise.

unknowns: Precise parameter estimation methods for non-stationary series
